audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Jacob/Esau encounter, bowing, embrace, face language, gift/blessing acceptance, reconciliation, Succoth, Shechem purchase, and El-Elohe-Israel altar.

verses.restored: Jacob lifted his eyes and saw, and look, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. He divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two slave-women.

familiar.text: And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau came...

modern.text: Now Jacob looked up and saw Esau coming toward him with four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two maidservants.

original.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה עֵשָׂ֣ו בָּ֔א וְעִמּ֕וֹ אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּ֣חַץ אֶת הַיְלָדִ֗ים עַל לֵאָה֙ וְעַל רָחֵ֔ל וְעַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֥י הַשְּׁפָחֽוֹת

verses.restored: He put the slave-women and their children first, Leah and her children after them, and Rachel and Joseph last.

familiar.text: And he put the handmaids and their children foremost...

notes.title: Household order
notes.body: The order reveals Jacob’s hierarchy of concern within the household.

modern.text: He put the maidservants and their children in front, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph at the rear.

original.text: וַיָּ֧שֶׂם אֶת הַשְּׁפָח֛וֹת וְאֶת יַלְדֵיהֶ֖ן רִֽאשֹׁנָ֑ה וְאֶת לֵאָ֤ה וִֽילָדֶ֨יהָ֙ אַחֲרֹנִ֔ים וְאֶת רָחֵ֥ל וְאֶת יוֹסֵ֖ף אַחֲרֹנִֽים

verses.restored: He himself passed over before them and bowed to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.

familiar.text: And he passed over before them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times...

modern.text: But Jacob himself went on ahead and bowed to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.

original.text: וְה֖וּא עָבַ֣ר לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֤חוּ אַ֨רְצָה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֔ים עַד גִּשְׁתּ֖וֹ עַד אָחִֽיו

verses.restored: Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, fell on his neck, kissed him, and they wept.

familiar.text: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him...

notes.title: Unexpected embrace
notes.body: The feared attack becomes embrace and tears.

modern.text: Esau, however, ran to him and embraced him, threw his arms around his neck, and kissed him. And they both wept.

original.text: וַיָּ֨רָץ עֵשָׂ֤ו לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ וַֽיְחַבְּקֵ֔הוּ וַיִּפֹּ֥ל עַל צַוָּארָ֖ו וַׄיִּׄשָּׁׄקֵ֑ׄהׄוּׄ וַיִּבְכּֽוּ

verses.restored: He lifted his eyes and saw the women and the children, and said, Who are these with you? He said, The children whom the Divine has graciously given your servant.

familiar.text: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children...

modern.text: When Esau looked up and saw the women and children, he asked, “Who are these with you?” Jacob answered, “These are the children God has graciously given your servant.”

original.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֣א אֶת עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּ֤רְא אֶת הַנָּשִׁים֙ וְאֶת הַיְלָדִ֔ים וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִי אֵ֣לֶּה לָּ֑ךְ וַיֹּאמַ֕ר הַיְלָדִ֕ים אֲשֶׁר חָנַ֥ן אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת עַבְדֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: The slave-women came near, they and their children, and bowed down.

familiar.text: Then the handmaidens came near, they and their children...

modern.text: Then the maidservants and their children approached and bowed down.

original.text: וַתִּגַּ֧שְׁןָ הַשְּׁפָח֛וֹת הֵ֥נָּה וְיַלְדֵיהֶ֖ן וַתִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶֽיןָ

verses.restored: Leah also came near with her children, and they bowed down. Afterward Joseph and Rachel came near, and they bowed down.

familiar.text: And Leah also with her children came near...

modern.text: Leah and her children also approached and bowed down, and then Joseph and Rachel approached and bowed down.

original.text: וַתִּגַּ֧שׁ גַּם לֵאָ֛ה וִילָדֶ֖יהָ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֑וּ וְאַחַ֗ר נִגַּ֥שׁ יוֹסֵ֛ף וְרָחֵ֖ל וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֽוּ

verses.restored: He said, What do you mean by all this camp that I met? He said, To find favor in the eyes of my lord.

familiar.text: And he said, What meanest thou by all this drove which I met?...

modern.text: “What do you mean by sending this whole company to meet me?” asked Esau. “To find favor in your sight, my lord,” Jacob answered.

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֥י לְךָ֛ כָּל הַמַּחֲנֶ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּגָ֑שְׁתִּי וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לִמְצֹא חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי

verses.restored: Esau said, I have much, my brother. Let what is yours be yours.

familiar.text: And Esau said, I have enough, my brother; keep that thou hast unto thyself.

modern.text: “I already have plenty, my brother,” Esau replied. “Keep what belongs to you.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר עֵשָׂ֖ו יֶשׁ לִ֣י רָ֑ב אָחִ֕י יְהִ֥י לְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁר לָֽךְ

verses.restored: Jacob said, No, please, if now I have found favor in your eyes, then take my gift from my hand, for I have seen your face as one sees the face of the Divine, and you have received me favorably.

familiar.text: And Jacob said, Nay, I pray thee, if now I have found grace...

notes.title: Face of the Divine
notes.body: After Peniel, Jacob sees Esau’s reconciled face as like seeing the Divine face.

modern.text: But Jacob insisted, “No, please! If I have found favor in your sight, then receive this gift from my hand. For indeed, I have seen your face, and it is like seeing the face of God, since you have received me favorably.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֗ב אַל נָא֙ אִם נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ מִנְחָתִ֖י מִיָּדִ֑י כִּ֣י עַל כֵּ֞ן רָאִ֣יתִי פָנֶ֗יךָ כִּרְאֹ֛ת פְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים וַתִּרְצֵֽנִי

verses.restored: Please take my blessing that has been brought to you, because the Divine has dealt graciously with me and because I have everything. He urged him, and he took it.

familiar.text: Take, I pray thee, my blessing that is brought to thee...

notes.title: My blessing
notes.body: Jacob gives a blessing/gift back to Esau, symbolically answering the stolen blessing story.

modern.text: Please accept my gift that was brought to you, because God has been gracious to me and I have all I need.” So Jacob pressed him until he accepted.

original.text: קַח נָ֤א אֶת בִּרְכָתִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֻבָ֣את לָ֔ךְ כִּֽי חַנַּ֥נִי אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְכִ֣י יֶשׁ לִי כֹ֑ל וַיִּפְצַר בּ֖וֹ וַיִּקָּֽח

verses.restored: He said, Let us journey and go, and I will go before you.

familiar.text: And he said, Let us take our journey, and let us go...

modern.text: Then Esau said, “Let us be on our way, and I will go ahead of you.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר נִסְעָ֣ה וְנֵלֵ֑כָה וְאֵלְכָ֖ה לְנֶגְדֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: He said to him, My lord knows that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds nursing are with me. If they are driven hard one day, all the flocks will die.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, My lord knoweth that the children are tender...

modern.text: But Jacob replied, “My lord knows that the children are frail, and I must care for sheep and cattle that are nursing their young. If they are driven hard for even a day, all the animals will die.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אֲדֹנִ֤י יֹדֵ֨עַ֙ כִּֽי הַיְלָדִ֣ים רַכִּ֔ים וְהַצֹּ֥אן וְהַבָּקָ֖ר עָל֣וֹת עָלָ֑י וּדְפָקוּם֙ י֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד וָמֵ֖תוּ כָּל הַצֹּֽאן

verses.restored: Please let my lord pass over before his servant, and I will lead on slowly, according to the pace of the livestock before me and the pace of the children, until I come to my lord in Seir.

familiar.text: Let my lord, I pray thee, pass over before his servant...

modern.text: Please let my lord go ahead of his servant. I will continue on slowly, at a comfortable pace for the livestock and children, until I come to my lord at Seir.”

original.text: יַעֲבָר נָ֥א אֲדֹנִ֖י לִפְנֵ֣י עַבְדּ֑וֹ וַאֲנִ֞י אֶֽתְנָהֲלָ֣ה לְאִטִּ֗י לְרֶ֨גֶל הַמְּלָאכָ֤ה אֲשֶׁר לְפָנַי֙ וּלְרֶ֣גֶל הַיְלָדִ֔ים עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר אָבֹ֥א אֶל אֲדֹנִ֖י שֵׂעִֽירָה

verses.restored: Esau said, Please let me leave with you some of the people who are with me. He said, Why this? Let me find favor in the eyes of my lord.

familiar.text: And Esau said, Let me now leave with thee some of the folk...

modern.text: “Let me leave some of my people with you,” Esau said. But Jacob replied, “Why do that? Let me find favor in the sight of my lord.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר עֵשָׂ֔ו אַצִּֽיגָה נָּ֣א עִמְּךָ֔ מִן הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתִּ֑י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לָ֣מָּה זֶּ֔ה אֶמְצָא חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי

verses.restored: So Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.

familiar.text: So Esau returned that day on his way unto Seir.

modern.text: So that day Esau started on his way back to Seir,

original.text: וַיָּשָׁב֩ בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֥וּא עֵשָׂ֛ו לְדַרְכּ֖וֹ שֵׂעִֽירָה

verses.restored: Jacob journeyed to Succoth, built himself a house, and made booths for his livestock. Therefore the name of the place was called Succoth.

familiar.text: And Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and built him an house...

modern.text: but Jacob went on to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and shelters for his livestock; that is why the place was called Succoth. Jacob Settles in Shechem

original.text: וְיַעֲקֹב֙ נָסַ֣ע סֻכֹּ֔תָה וַיִּ֥בֶן ל֖וֹ בָּ֑יִת וּלְמִקְנֵ֨הוּ֙ עָשָׂ֣ה סֻכֹּ֔ת עַל כֵּ֛ן קָרָ֥א שֵׁם הַמָּק֖וֹם סֻכּֽוֹת

verses.restored: Jacob came in peace to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan-Aram, and he camped before the city.

familiar.text: And Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem...

notes.title: In peace / Shalem
notes.body: The Hebrew may be read as safely/in peace or as Shalem, a place-name. This rendering preserves the peace motif after Jacob’s vow.

modern.text: After Jacob had come from Paddan-aram, he arrived safely at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan, and he camped just outside the city.

original.text: וַיָּבֹא֩ יַעֲקֹ֨ב שָׁלֵ֜ם עִ֣יר שְׁכֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן בְּבֹא֖וֹ מִפַּדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֑ם וַיִּ֖חַן אֶת פְּנֵ֥י הָעִֽיר

verses.restored: He bought the portion of the field where he had stretched his tent from the hand of the sons of Hamor, father of Shechem, for one hundred qesitah.

familiar.text: And he bought a parcel of a field...

modern.text: And the plot of ground where he pitched his tent, he purchased from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for a hundred pieces of silver.

original.text: וַיִּ֜קֶן אֶת חֶלְקַ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽטָה שָׁם֙ אָהֳל֔וֹ מִיַּ֥ד בְּנֵֽי חֲמ֖וֹר אֲבִ֣י שְׁכֶ֑ם בְּמֵאָ֖ה קְשִׂיטָֽה

verses.restored: He set up an altar there and called it El-Elohe-Israel, God, the Divine of Israel.

familiar.text: And he erected there an altar, and called it EleloheIsrael.

notes.title: El-Elohe-Israel
notes.body: The altar name links Jacob’s new name Israel with the Divine.

modern.text: There he set up an altar and called it El-Elohe-Israel.

original.text: וַיַּצֶּב שָׁ֖ם מִזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּ֨קְרָא ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ל אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
